chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, when two Muslims meet, the superior of the two is the one who has more intense love for his companion.

key_terms.أَشَدُّهُمَا: The more intense/stronger of the two

ai.seo_question: What determines which of two Muslims is superior when they meet?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links spiritual rank directly to interpersonal affection, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *mawaddah* (love) as a tangible manifestation of faith. This criterion underscores that true piety is not merely ritualistic but is expressed through the warmth and sincerity one extends to fellow believers, a concept central to the *Ahl al-Bayt*'s teachings on social ethics.
